title: Champions League Predictions: Man Utd, Barcelona Face Tough Away Gigs, Arsenal at Home
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackOct 12, 2026Barcelona made a red-hot start to this season’s Champions League—but they won’t have Raphinha available for Matchday 2.  / Judit Cartiel/Getty Images More than a month has passed since the 2026–27 Champions League got underway, with an extended international break meaning we’re easing back into the new season after a rather brief opening act.

And while players will again convene with their national teams next month, Europe’s premier club competition finds its groove over the coming weeks, as the continent’s elite vie to place themselves toward the summit in a bid to avoid two extra games in the new year.
Matchday 1 was split across three evenings, and we’re back to two sets of nine matches until the chaotic final slate of league phase fixtures.
Here’s how Sports Illustrated predicts Tuesday’s Matchday 2 games to play out.

A dip seemed inevitable for Lens this season, given the turnover in the summer off the back of a second-place Ligue 1 finish. They’ve already parted ways with Pierre Sage’s successor, Dino Toppmöller, and are now being led by the inexperienced Yannick Cahuzac.

Cahuzac did oversee a domestic victory over Lyon at the weekend, and the French club are targeting back-to-back wins to start their league phase campaign. They’re unlikely to prevail quite as dramatically as they did on Matchday 1, when two stoppage-time goals saw Les Sang et Or overturn a 2–1 deficit at Slavia Prague.

Sporting CP are seasoned in this competition, and were quarterfinalists last time out after stunning Bodø/Glimt in the second leg of their round of 16 tie. The Primeira Liga side are unbeaten so far this term, but a habit of drawing has left them third in the league through eight games. Galatasaray were cast aside during their league phase opener.
Competition debutants Sabah had quite the welcome on Matchday 1, and they offered a pretty admirable account of themselves at Old Trafford, even in a 4–0 defeat.
Sabah will find points hard to come by during their maiden league phase campaign, but they’ll surely view this fixture as a huge opportunity to claim a first Champions League victory.

Slavia remain dominant domestically, but hardly rank among Europe’s top dogs. Their frailties, even at home, were laid bare on Matchday 1, capitulating against Lens. The visitors are facing a Sabah team that’s won seven straight on home soil, with Valdas Dambrauskas’s side likely to be buoyed by the occasion.
Arsenal saw off Napoli on Matchday 1.  / Alberto Lingria/Xinhua/Getty ImagesPrediction: Arsenal 3–1 Lille

Arsenal’s quest to complete their linear progression in this competition started with a convincing victory in Naples. On another night, the Gunners would’ve ran out emphatic winners, but a profligate showing from Mikel Arteta‘s side meant Martin Ødegaard’s second-half strike proved the difference.

While questions continue to be raised regarding the potency of Arsenal’s frontline, it’s evident that they’ve acquired a difference-maker in midfield. Bruno Guimarães was again decisive off the bench at the weekend, helping Arsenal overturn a home deficit to Leeds United.

The Brazilian will be expected to showcase his best under the bright lights on Champions League nights, and while Lille have enjoyed a strong start to their domestic campaign, the Ligue 1 side, with a 40-year-old Olivier Giroud leading their line, is unlikely to compete fiercely with the Premier League champions.

The pressure certainly didn’t ease on Michael Carrick after Saturday’s draw at home to Tottenham Hotspur. Spurs were dominant at Old Trafford against a Manchester United team bereft of energy, and were unfortunate to leave the Theatre of Dreams with just a point.
The game was there for the Red Devils after Bryan Mbuemo’s strike and Rodrigo Bentancur’s red card, but Dominic Solanke bullied Lisandro Martínez late on to head home and earn the visitors a point.
A daunting test welcomes Man Utd next, with Atlético Madrid heading into Tuesday’s bout off the back of a four-game winning run since they were beaten at Anfield on Matchday 1.
Atléti seldom lose at the Metropolitano, and the United we've seen at the start of 2026–27 doesn’t look like a team capable of producing a brave away performance garnering a victory.

Hansi Flick’s juggernaut was at it again upon their return from the extended break. There’s no one in La Liga that can compete with Barcelona right now, and Getafe were merely the last to succumb to their every whim.
